processing: Buds or one bud with a just-opening leaf are fixed at high temperature, lightly rolled, shaped and dried, then trimmed of fines before storage.
harvest_season: Spring, as buds or one bud with one just-opening leaf.
appearance_dry: Tight, straight, fine strands, glossy green with visible white down.
appearance_liquor: Clear and bright, typically a pale yellow-green.
taste_profile: A clean, elegant aroma with a fresh, mellow and clean-tasting body.

brewing.notes: These are usual settings for a bud-heavy green. Too much heat flattens the aroma, so let the water cool first.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring harvest, like other bud-picked Jiangsu greens, and best drunk within a year. Earlier lots usually fetch more. It is not an ageing tea.
description:
Yangxian Xueya, snow bud of Yangxian, is a green tea from the hilly south of Yixing, near Lake Tai. It is the modern face of the old Yangxian tea name.

It is made from buds or a bud with one just-opening leaf, from cultivars such as Chuye and Zhenong 139. High-heat fixing, light rolling and shaping give tight, straight, fine strands with visible white down, and the fines are trimmed away before storage.

The cup is clear and bright, with a clean aroma and a fresh, mellow taste. Use water around 80 °C and short steeps; a glass shows off the shoots.

The name is a registered geographical indication, so look for the Yixing origin and the harvest year.
history:
The name comes from a line by Su Shi about seeking snow buds in Yangxian. The verse supplied the name, but nothing shows he had anything to do with this tea's method. The tea is best read as a modern product built on Yixing's Tang tribute reputation.

It was registered as a Chinese agricultural geographical indication in 2010, with the Yixing tea industry association as certificate holder. Little is documented in accessible form about the year and people behind its creation.
